
#======================================================================================================
Causal analysis of ecology, subsistence composition, and social organization in trans-historical small-scale farming societies using mixed-type Bayesian networks

## Supplementary analysis: discrete Bayesian network
## All continuous variables are discretized (median split or tertiles)

Rosy Oh and Man-Suk Oh


Oct 26, 2026

#======================================================================================================

Variant of main.rmd in which all continuous variables (5 ecology, 4 ALR subsistence
variables, CommSize) are discretized, so that every node is categorical and a discrete BN
is learned with the G-square CI test (disCItest) instead of mixCItest.

Pipeline
  1. Read data and pre-process
  2. Discretize continuous variables (median split or tertiles)
  3. Build the blacklist (same as main.rmd)
  4. Learn BN structures on bootstrap samples with tpc() + disCItest;
     Arc strength / direction; select arcs
  5. build the consensus DAG
  6. Fit local models (multinomial logistic regression for every node)
  7. Interventional analysis: P(X = k | do(Y = j)) via Monte Carlo simulation
  8. BIC of the consensus DAG

Required folders: data/ (input csv) and output/ (results). Run from the repository root.
Output file names contain "disc_<disc_method>" so that results of main.rmd are not overwritten.



# Install packages (installs only packages that are missing)
```{r}
# ── Bioconductor packages (not available on CRAN) ──────────────────────────────
bioc_req <- c("graph", "RBGL", "Rgraphviz")
bioc_missing <- setdiff(bioc_req, rownames(installed.packages()))

if (length(bioc_missing) > 0) {
  if (!require("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("BiocManager")

  BiocManager::install(bioc_missing)
}

# ── CRAN packages ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
cran_req <- c(
  "pcalg",    # PC algorithm-based causal discovery; disCItest (G-square test)
  "bnlearn",  # Bayesian network learning
  "tpc",      # tpc() algorithm

```



# 0. Load packages
```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(pcalg)
  library(Rgraphviz)
  library(bnlearn)
  library(tpc)
  library(nnet)
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyverse)
})
```



# 1. Read data and pre-process
```{r}

# ── Analysis options ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# disc_method : discretization of continuous variables
#               "median"  two categories (Low / High), split at the median
#               "tertile" three categories (Low / Medium / High), split at tertiles
# direction   : blacklist scenario
#               "none"        no ordering between Subsistence and SocialOrg
#               "sub_to_soc"  Subsistence -> SocialOrg only
#               "soc_to_sub"  SocialOrg -> Subsistence only
# threshold   : minimum arc strength for the consensus DAG
# B           : number of bootstrap replicates
disc_method = "median"
direction   = "none"
threshold   = 0.3
B           = 10000

# Label used in output file names, e.g. "disc_median_none_thr3"
tag <- paste0("disc_", disc_method, "_", direction, "_thr", as.integer(threshold * 10))


# Input data: first column = society ID, then 5 Ecology, 4 Subsistence and
# 4 SocialOrg variables (in this order)
dat.score=read.csv("data/dat_score_ALR_agri_157.csv",  header = TRUE)

names(dat.score)
dat.score=dat.score[, -1, drop=F]  # drop the Society ID column
Ecology=names(dat.score)[1:5]
Subsistence=names(dat.score)[6:9]
SocialOrg=names(dat.score)[10:13]


# Merge the "Camp" settlement type into "Hamlet"
dat.score$SettlementType[dat.score$SettlementType == "Camp"] <- "Hamlet"
dat.score$SettlementType <- factor(dat.score$SettlementType)

# Categorical social organization variables as factors
SocialOrg_categorical <- c("SettlementType", "CommOrg", "HouseholdOrg")
dat.score[SocialOrg_categorical] <- lapply(dat.score[SocialOrg_categorical], factor)

```



# 2. Discretize all continuous variables
```{r}
# Continuous variables: 5 ecology, 4 ALR subsistence, CommSize (10 in total)
cont_vars <- names(dat.score)[sapply(dat.score, is.numeric)]
print(cont_vars)

# Median split: values above the median -> "High"; ties at the median -> "Low"
dichotomize_median <- function(x) {
  m <- median(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  factor(ifelse(x > m, "High", "Low"), levels = c("Low", "High"))
}

# Tertile split: Low / Medium / High
# (fewer categories, with a warning, if tertile cutoffs are tied)
tertile_cut <- function(x) {
  br <- quantile(x, probs = c(0, 1/3, 2/3, 1), na.rm = TRUE, type = 7)
  if (any(duplicated(br))) {
    warning("Tied tertile cutoffs; fewer than 3 categories: ", paste(round(br, 3), collapse = ", "))
    br <- unique(br)
  }
  labs <- c("Low", "Medium", "High")[seq_len(length(br) - 1)]
  cut(x, breaks = br, labels = labs, include.lowest = TRUE, right = TRUE)
}

disc_fun <- if (disc_method == "median") dichotomize_median else tertile_cut

dat.trans <- dat.score
dat.trans[cont_vars] <- lapply(dat.score[cont_vars], disc_fun)

# Check category sizes and the number of ties at the median
sapply(dat.trans[cont_vars], table)
sapply(dat.score[cont_vars], function(x) sum(x == median(x)))

# All variables must now be factors
stopifnot(all(sapply(dat.trans, is.factor)))

```



# 3. Blacklist (forbidden arcs) — same constraints as main.rmd
```{r}

# forb_all[a, b] = TRUE forbids the arc a -> b
# (scenario set by `direction` in Section 1)

forb_all <- matrix(
  FALSE,
  nrow = ncol(dat.trans),
  ncol = ncol(dat.trans),
  dimnames = list(names(dat.trans), names(dat.trans))
)

# Ecology is exogenous: no arcs from Subsistence or SocialOrg into Ecology
forb_all[Subsistence, Ecology] <- TRUE
forb_all[SocialOrg, Ecology] <- TRUE

# Scenario-specific constraints between Subsistence and SocialOrg
if( direction == "sub_to_soc"){
   forb_all[SocialOrg, Subsistence] <- TRUE
} else if ( direction == "soc_to_sub"){
   forb_all[Subsistence, SocialOrg] <- TRUE
}
# if direction == "none" : no constraints


# No arcs among subsistence variables: avoid spurious arcs induced by the common ALR reference (Agriculture)
forb_all[Subsistence, Subsistence] <- TRUE


diag(forb_all) <- FALSE

# Ecology hierarchy:
# Geography -> Topography -> Climate
Geography  <- c("DistanceCoast", "Elevation")
Topography <- "Slope"
Climate    <- c("AnnualTemp", "MonthlyPrecip")

# No arc between the two geographic variables (both directions forbidden):
# DistanceCoast and Elevation are both exogenous features of location, and
# neither causes the other.
forb_all["DistanceCoast", "Elevation"] <- TRUE
forb_all["Elevation", "DistanceCoast"] <- TRUE

# Forbid reverse directions within the hierarchy
forb_all[Topography, Geography] <- TRUE
forb_all[Climate, Geography] <- TRUE
forb_all[Climate, Topography] <- TRUE

# Arrange data and blacklist in exactly the same variable order
cols <- c(Ecology, SocialOrg, Subsistence)

dat <- dat.trans %>%   select(all_of(cols))

forb <- forb_all[cols, cols]

stopifnot(
  identical(names(dat), rownames(forb)),
  identical(names(dat), colnames(forb))
)

```



# 4. Learn BN structure on bootstrap samples; arc strength and arc selection
```{r}

# Fit a single discrete BN to one bootstrap sample with tpc()
# disCItest (G-square test) requires
#   dm   : integer matrix with categories coded 0, 1, ..., nlev - 1
#   nlev : number of levels of each variable (taken from the factor levels, so
#          that a level absent from a bootstrap sample is still counted)
fit_one <- function(dat_sub, forb, alpha_level, numCores) {

  dm   <- as.matrix(dat_sub %>% mutate(across(everything(), ~ as.integer(.x) - 1L)))
  nlev <- sapply(dat_sub, nlevels)

  fit <- tpc(
    suffStat    = list(dm = dm, nlev = nlev, adaptDF = FALSE),
    indepTest   = disCItest,      # G-square CI test for discrete data
    labels      = names(dat_sub),
    alpha       = alpha_level,    # significance level of the CI tests
    forbEdges   = forb,           # blacklist matrix (domain constraints)
    maj.rule    = TRUE,           # majority rule for edge orientation
    skel.method = "stable",
    numCores    = 1
  )
  return(fit)
}

# ── Bootstrap settings ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
set.seed(2374)

#B  : number of bootstrap replicates (set in Section 1)
p   <- ncol(dat)
vn  <- names(dat)

# Storage: only DAGs that convert without cycles are kept
boot_nets        <- list()
successful_boots <- 0
skipped_boots    <- c()     # indices of replicates that failed conversion (e.g. cycles)

# ── Main bootstrap loop ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
t0 <- Sys.time()

for (b in 1:B) {

  # Resample 80% of the observations (sampling with replacement)
  idx <- sample.int(
    nrow(dat),
    size = floor(0.8 * nrow(dat)),
    replace = TRUE
  )

  # Suppress warnings from sparse contingency tables in disCItest()
  fit <- suppressWarnings(
    fit_one(dat[idx, , drop = FALSE],
            forb = forb,
            alpha_level = 0.1     )
  )

  # Convert to a bnlearn "bn" object; skip the replicate if it contains a cycle
  tryCatch({
    g <- as.bn(fit, check.cycles = TRUE)
    successful_boots <- successful_boots + 1
    boot_nets[[successful_boots]] <- g
  }, error = function(e) {
    cat("Bootstrap", b, "conversion failed:",
        conditionMessage(e), "\n")
    skipped_boots <<- c(skipped_boots, b)
  })

}
cat("Finished bootstrap:", b,
    "Elapsed:",
    round(as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), t0,
                              units = "secs")), 1),
    "seconds\n")
flush.console()

cat(sprintf("Completed: %d/%d replicates accepted (%d skipped)\n",
            successful_boots, B, length(skipped_boots)))

# ── Arc strength and direction (fn_calculate_arc_strength.R) ────────────────
source("fn_calculate_arc_strength.R")
arc_strength <- calculate_arc_strength(boot_nets, vn)

summary(arc_strength$strength) # strength and direction are both in [0, 1]


# ── Arc selection ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Keep arcs with strength >= threshold and direction >= 0.5
selected_arcs <- arc_strength[
  arc_strength$strength  >= threshold &
    arc_strength$direction >= 0.5, ]
print(selected_arcs)

n_arcs <- nrow(selected_arcs);n_arcs


# Save selected arcs and all arc strengths
write.csv(selected_arcs, paste0("output/disc_selected_arcs_", tag, ".csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(arc_strength,  paste0("output/disc_arc_strength_",  tag, ".csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```



# 5. Construct the consensus DAG from the selected arcs
```{r}

# Start from an empty graph on all nodes
avg_graph <- empty.graph(vn)

# Add selected arcs one by one, skipping any that would create a cycle
for (k in 1:nrow(selected_arcs)) {
  test_graph <- set.arc(avg_graph,
                        from         = as.character(selected_arcs$from[k]),
                        to           = as.character(selected_arcs$to[k]),
                        check.cycles = FALSE)

  if (acyclic(test_graph, directed = TRUE)) {
    avg_graph <- test_graph
  } else {
    message("Skipped arc: ", selected_arcs$from[k], " -> ",
            selected_arcs$to[k], " (would create cycle)")
  }
}

# Remove isolated nodes (keep only nodes involved in at least one arc)
connected_nodes <- unique(c(arcs(avg_graph)[, "from"], arcs(avg_graph)[, "to"]))
avg_graph <- bnlearn::subgraph(avg_graph, connected_nodes)
cat("Number of arcs in consensus DAG:", narcs(avg_graph), "\n")


# Keep a copy named by method and scenario, e.g. avg_graph_disc_median_none_thr3
assign(paste0("avg_graph_", tag), avg_graph)

# Label for output files of Sections 7-8 (changed by fn_sensitivity_analysis.R for M1-M3)
out_label <- direction


# Save / reload the consensus DAG (uncomment as needed)
#fname=paste0("avg_graph_", tag, ".rds")
#saveRDS(avg_graph, file =fname, compress = TRUE)
#avg_graph <- readRDS(fname)


# ── Plot the consensus DAG ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

gR <- graphviz.plot(avg_graph, shape = "rectangle")

# ── Node appearance ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
node.attrs <- nodeRenderInfo(gR)
arc.attrs  <- edgeRenderInfo(gR)

# Global node style
node.attrs$col     <- "black"
node.attrs$textCol <- "black"
node.attrs$fontsize <- 14

# Node fill colours by variable group
node.attrs$fill[c(Geography, Topography)] <- "lightgray"    # geography and topography
node.attrs$fill[Climate]                  <- "lightyellow"  # climate
node.attrs$fill[Subsistence]              <- "lightgreen"   # subsistence strategies
node.attrs$fill[SocialOrg]                <- "lightblue"    # social organisation

nodeRenderInfo(gR) <- node.attrs

# ── Arc appearance ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Arcs with direction < 0.60: dashed (weak directional consensus)
# Arcs with direction >= 0.60: solid  (strong directional consensus)
all_arc_names <- names(arc.attrs$lty)

for (k in 1:nrow(selected_arcs)) {
  arc_name <- paste0(selected_arcs$from[k], "~", selected_arcs$to[k])

  if (arc_name %in% all_arc_names) {
    arc.attrs$col[arc_name] <- "black"
    arc.attrs$lwd[arc_name] <- 2
    arc.attrs$lty[arc_name] <- ifelse(selected_arcs$direction[k] < 0.6,
                                      "dashed", "solid")
    arc.attrs$fontsize[arc_name] <- 10
  }
}

edgeRenderInfo(gR) <- arc.attrs
renderGraph(gR)


# ── Save plots (TIFF, PNG, PDF) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
filename <- paste0("output/BN_", tag)

tiff(paste0(filename, ".tif"), res = 300, width = 15, height = 10,
     units = "cm", compression = "lzw", bg = "white", type = "cairo")
renderGraph(gR)
dev.off()

png(paste0(filename, ".png"), res = 300, width = 15, height = 10,
    units = "cm", bg = "transparent")
renderGraph(gR)
dev.off()

pdf(paste0(filename, ".pdf"))
renderGraph(gR)
dev.off()
```
